questions.explanation: Small livestock such as rabbits, snails and grasscutters need little space and capital.

questions.topic: Methods of Weed and Pest Control
questions.stem: A weed is
options: a plant growing where it is not wanted
questions.explanation: Any plant growing where it is not wanted is a weed.

questions.topic: Methods of Weed and Pest Control
questions.stem: Which of these is a characteristic of weeds?
options: They produce no seeds at all
They produce many seeds that are easily dispersed
They need a lot of care to survive
They grow slowly and die easily
questions.explanation: Weeds survive well because they produce many seeds that spread easily.

questions.topic: Methods of Weed and Pest Control
questions.stem: Chemicals used to kill weeds are called
questions.explanation: Herbicides kill weeds; insecticides kill insects.

questions.topic: Methods of Weed and Pest Control

questions.explanation: Aphids pierce plant tissues and suck the sap.

questions.topic: Methods of Weed and Pest Control
questions.stem: Grasshoppers damage crops mainly by

questions.topic: Methods of Weed and Pest Control
questions.stem: Some weeds are useful. Which of the following is a use of certain weeds?
options: They remove pests from the farm
Some are used as medicine or animal feed
questions.explanation: Some weeds have medicinal value or can be eaten by livestock.

questions.topic: Methods of Weed and Pest Control
questions.stem: A farmer sprays too much herbicide close to a stream. The most likely effect is
options: pollution of the water and harm to fish
faster growth of fish in the stream
more weeds along the stream banks
questions.explanation: Excess farm chemicals can wash into water and poison aquatic life and livestock.

questions.topic: Methods of Weed and Pest Control
questions.stem: Planting different crops on the same piece of land in a planned order each season helps to control weeds and pests. This practice is called
questions.explanation: Crop rotation breaks the life cycles of pests and weeds.

questions.topic: Methods of Weed and Pest Control
questions.stem: Pests reduce crop yield mainly by
options: damaging leaves, stems, roots or fruits
questions.explanation: Damaged plant parts lead to lower yield and poorer quality.

questions.stem: The factors of agricultural production include land, labour, capital (money) and
questions.explanation: Management (the entrepreneur) organises the other factors.

questions.stem: The human effort, physical or mental, used in farm production is called
questions.explanation: Labour is human effort in production.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of capital on a farm?
questions.explanation: Capital refers to man-made goods and money used in production, such as tractors.

questions.stem: Water is an important factor of agricultural production because
options: it increases the price of seeds
it reduces the need for land
crops and animals need it to grow and survive
questions.explanation: Without water, crops wilt and animals die.

questions.stem: A farm manager who decides what to plant, buys inputs, hires workers and sells the produce is performing the role of

questions.stem: Which factor of agricultural production is fixed in supply and cannot be moved from one place to another?
questions.explanation: Land is immobile and limited in supply.

questions.stem: A building used for storing grains such as maize after harvest is called a

questions.stem: Which of the following is a farm structure used for keeping poultry?
questions.explanation: Poultry can be kept in a deep litter house.

questions.explanation: Rabbits are kept in hutches.

questions.stem: A building used for keeping pigs is called a
questions.explanation: Pigs are housed in sties.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the BEST way to maintain a farm building?
options: Regular cleaning, repairing damaged parts and painting where necessary
Using it to store fuel and chemicals with animals
Leaving it unused for many years
Removing the roof during the rainy season
questions.explanation: Regular cleaning, repairs and painting make farm buildings last longer.

questions.stem: Why should a poultry house be built with its length running east to west?
options: To reduce direct sunlight entering the house
To keep the birds facing the market
To allow rain to enter the house
To make the house easier to paint
questions.explanation: An east-west orientation reduces direct sunlight and keeps the house cooler.

questions.stem: The process of reproducing or multiplying plants is called
questions.explanation: Propagation means producing new plants from seeds or plant parts.

questions.stem: Which of the following crops is usually propagated by stem cuttings?
questions.explanation: Cassava is planted from pieces of its stem.

questions.stem: Yam is commonly propagated by
questions.explanation: Farmers plant yam setts (cut pieces of tuber) or small whole tubers.

questions.stem: Plantain and banana are propagated mainly by
questions.explanation: Suckers growing from the base of the parent plant are used to raise new plantain.

questions.stem: Propagation by seed is also called
questions.explanation: Seeds result from fertilisation, so seed propagation is sexual.

questions.stem: One advantage of vegetative propagation is that
options: the new plants are exactly like the parent plant
the planting materials are very light to carry
questions.explanation: Plants raised from vegetative parts are identical to the parent.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a DISADVANTAGE of propagating crops by vegetative organs?
options: Diseases of the parent plant can be passed on to the new plants
The planting materials can be stored for many years
The new plants grow more slowly than seedlings
questions.explanation: Vegetative parts carry any disease the parent has.

questions.stem: A disadvantage of propagating crops by seed is that
options: seeds are too heavy to transport
the offspring may not be exactly like the parent
questions.explanation: Seedlings can vary from the parent because they come from sexual reproduction.

questions.stem: Removing trees, shrubs and grasses from a piece of land before planting is called
questions.explanation: Clearing is the first pre-planting operation.

questions.stem: Covering the soil surface around crops with dry grass or leaves is called
questions.explanation: Mulching conserves soil moisture and controls weeds.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a post-planting operation?
questions.explanation: Weeding is done after the crop has been planted.

questions.stem: Removing excess seedlings from a stand so that the remaining ones grow well is called
questions.explanation: Thinning reduces overcrowding.

questions.stem: Replacing seeds that failed to germinate with new ones is called
questions.explanation: Supplying fills gaps left by seeds that did not germinate.

questions.stem: A nursery is
options: a place where seedlings are raised
a place for selling farm produce
questions.explanation: Seedlings of crops like tomato and pepper are raised in a nursery.

questions.stem: A farmer plants maize on a plot measuring 20 m by 10 m at a spacing of 1 m by 0.5 m, with 2 seeds per hole. How many maize seeds does he need?
questions.explanation: Area = 200 m²; each stand takes 1 x 0.5 = 0.5 m², so 200 ÷ 0.5 = 400 stands; 400 x 2 seeds = 800 seeds.

questions.stem: A farmer plants 60 cowpea seeds and 45 of them germinate. What is the germination percentage?
questions.explanation: Germination percentage = 45 ÷ 60 x 100 = 75%.

questions.stem: What is the most likely effect of harvesting maize very late?
options: Pests, birds and rain damage the grains
The maize becomes sweeter and heavier
The grains germinate faster in storage
questions.explanation: Delayed harvesting exposes crops to pests, rodents, birds and rain damage.

questions.stem: Turning cassava tubers into garri is an example of
questions.explanation: Processing crops into usable forms is a post-harvest operation.

questions.stem: Treating seeds with a chemical before planting is mainly done to
options: make the seeds heavier for planting
protect them from soil pests and diseases
change their colour for easy sale
stop them from germinating too early
questions.explanation: Seed dressing protects seeds from soil pests and fungi.

questions.stem: Feed can be defined as
options: the bedding in an animal house
questions.explanation: Feed is the food that farm animals eat.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a protein-yielding feed?
questions.explanation: Groundnut cake is rich in protein.

questions.stem: Maize, cassava and millet are used in animal feed mainly as sources of
questions.explanation: Cereals and cassava supply carbohydrate, which gives energy.

questions.stem: The container in which water is provided for poultry is called a
questions.explanation: Drinkers supply water to birds.

questions.stem: A long, open container from which animals eat their feed is called a
questions.explanation: Troughs hold feed or water for livestock.

questions.stem: A poultry farmer has 100 birds, and each bird eats 120 g of feed per day. How much feed will the birds eat in one week?
questions.explanation: 100 x 120 g = 12,000 g per day = 12 kg; 12 kg x 7 days = 84 kg.

questions.stem: Which of the following feed ingredients is a good source of protein of animal origin?
questions.explanation: Fish meal comes from fish and is very rich in protein.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a viral disease of poultry?

questions.stem: Which of the following is a sign that a farm animal is sick?
questions.explanation: Sick animals often refuse to eat.

questions.stem: Trypanosomiasis in cattle is spread by the

questions.stem: Coccidiosis in poultry is caused by a

questions.stem: Bloat in ruminants is classified as a

questions.stem: Which of these is a fungal disease of farm animals?
questions.explanation: Despite its name, ringworm is caused by a fungus.

questions.stem: Keeping a newly bought animal away from the rest of the herd for some days before mixing them is called

questions.stem: A farmer had 500 broilers and lost 4% of them to disease. How many broilers were left?
questions.explanation: 4% of 500 = 20 birds; 500 - 20 = 480 birds left.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the BEST way to prevent viral diseases such as Newcastle disease in poultry?
options: Vaccinating the birds at the right time
Keeping the birds in dark houses
questions.explanation: Viral diseases are prevented by vaccination; antibiotics do not kill viruses.

questions.stem: One effect of disease on farm animals is
questions.explanation: Sick animals grow poorly and produce less.

questions.stem: Fishery can be defined as
options: the rearing of snails for meat
the catching and rearing of fish
the growing of rice in swamps
the keeping of bees for honey
questions.explanation: Fishery covers catching, rearing and managing fish and other aquatic animals.

questions.stem: Tilapia and catfish are examples of
questions.explanation: Tilapia and catfish live in rivers, lakes and ponds.

questions.stem: A shark is classified as a
questions.explanation: Sharks have skeletons made of cartilage.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a method of catching fish?
questions.explanation: Hook and line, nets and traps are fishing methods.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a use of fish?
options: It is used as fuel for cars
It is used to make cement
It is used to make paper
It is a source of protein for humans
questions.explanation: Fish is an important source of protein; fish meal is also used in animal feed.

questions.stem: Using chemicals to kill fish for sale is dangerous mainly because
options: the water becomes cleaner for other fish
the chemicals can poison people who eat the fish
more fish are hatched in the river
the fish grow faster and become too big

questions.stem: Crabs, shrimps and periwinkles are examples of

options: Feeding fish with good quality feed
Stocking the pond at the right density
Draining industrial waste into the pond
questions.explanation: Industrial effluent pollutes water and can kill fish.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a forest resource?

questions.stem: A forest with many tall trees, thick undergrowth and heavy rainfall throughout most of the year is the

questions.stem: A forest with few trees that developed after the original forest was cleared by man is called a

options: They protect the soil from erosion

questions.stem: Which of the following is the BEST way to reduce the effects of deforestation in Nigeria?
questions.explanation: Planting trees restores forest cover and protects the environment.

questions.stem: Palm oil is best packaged in

liquid or solid, and its shape

questions.stem: Eggs are best packaged for sale in

questions.stem: Why is distance to the market an important packaging criterion?
options: Produce travelling far does not need packaging
Short distances require more expensive packages
Produce travelling far needs stronger packaging to avoid damage
questions.explanation: The longer the journey, the more protection the produce needs.

questions.stem: Frozen fish being sent from Lagos to Kaduna would be BEST packaged in

supply is low while demand remains high

questions.stem: Making the public aware of a product through radio, posters or social media in order to sell it is called
questions.explanation: Advertising informs and persuades buyers.

questions.stem: Farm records are

the songs farmers sing at work
the tools used on a farm

options: To know whether the farm is making a profit or loss
To increase the price of fertilizer

the keeping of books in a library

questions.stem: One benefit of keeping farm records on a computer is that
options: records can be stored safely and retrieved quickly
the farm no longer needs a manager
records can never be lost under any condition
it increases rainfall on the farm
questions.explanation: Computers make storing, updating and finding records easier.

questions.stem: A stock exchange is
options: a market for selling livestock only
a store for keeping farm produce
a bank that gives loans to farmers only
a market where shares and securities are bought and sold
questions.explanation: Shares of companies are traded on the stock exchange.

questions.stem: The person who buys and sells shares on behalf of clients on the stock exchange is called a
questions.explanation: Stockbrokers act as agents for buyers and sellers of shares.

questions.stem: One importance of the stock exchange to agriculture is that it
questions.explanation: Agro-allied companies raise money by selling shares to investors.

questions.stem: The main stock exchange in Nigeria is located in

questions.stem: Export promotion means
options: encouraging the sale of local goods abroad
selling goods only within a village

questions.stem: Which of the following is a major Nigerian agricultural export?
questions.explanation: Cocoa is an important agricultural export; crude oil and tin are minerals.

questions.stem: One benefit of agricultural export promotion to Nigeria is that it
questions.explanation: Exports bring in foreign currency.

questions.stem: How does export promotion benefit Nigerian farmers directly?
options: It reduces the prices of their produce
It increases the cost of their inputs
It provides additional markets for their produce

questions.explanation: The NEPC promotes non-oil exports, including agricultural produce.

questions.topic: Puberty, Adolescence, Sexually Transmitted Infections (STI) and Human Rights
questions.stem: Puberty is the stage of life when

questions.topic: Puberty, Adolescence, Sexually Transmitted Infections (STI) and Human Rights

questions.explanation: Menstruation is a key sign of puberty in girls.

questions.explanation: Boys' voices become deeper during puberty.

questions.stem: Adolescence is best described as the period
options: when a person is a baby

questions.topic: Puberty, Adolescence, Sexually Transmitted Infections (STI) and Human Rights

questions.explanation: Adolescents are often pressured by friends to behave in certain ways.

options: sharing unsterilised needles and sharp objects
eating together from the same plate

questions.stem: Things a family must have in order to survive, such as food, clothing and shelter, are called

questions.explanation: A television is desirable but not necessary for survival.

questions.stem: A family goal can be defined as

measures used to judge how well goals are achieved
the things a family wants but does not need
the money and property of the family
questions.explanation: Standards measure how well something has been done.

options: Needs lead to goals, and standards measure their achievement
Goals and standards mean the same as wants
Needs, goals and standards are not related
Standards are set before any needs exist

questions.stem: Time, energy, knowledge and skills are examples of
questions.explanation: Human resources come from people themselves.

questions.stem: Money, land and household equipment are examples of

questions.stem: Decision making is
options: choosing the best option from alternatives
spending all one's money at once
questions.explanation: Decision making means choosing between alternatives.

questions.stem: The FIRST step in decision making is to
questions.explanation: You must know the problem before you can solve it.

questions.stem: Public libraries, parks and health centres are examples of

buy the mathematical set first because it is a need

Very low prices of all goods

report the seller to the army

options: getting a refund, repair or replacement
